Subject: Follow-up: prompt output PII — storage, residency, and TTL Q&A

Hi Maria — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the items we said we'd follow up on so your security/privacy team has clear answers: 

1) What we store by default for hosted API: request metadata (timestamp, model id, route), prompts/inputs are not persisted unless you opt in or enable debug/logging; by default prompt text is not stored beyond short-lived telemetry used for routing.
2) Prompt outputs: ephemeral by default for session-based calls. If you enable "persist outputs" we persist encrypted output blobs for debugging and evals.
3) Retention: default telemetry/rolling logs retained 30 days; persisted outputs (if enabled) retained configurable up to 90 days for hosted customers. Dedicated/Private customers can set retention to customer policy or opt for zero retention.
4) Residency: data region selectable at account level (us / eu / apac). Hosted defaults to us-east unless you request eu region during onboarding.
5) Controls: customer-managed KMS, option to disable persistent logging, audit logs (13 months retention by default), and exportable logs for compliance.

Attaching a lightweight diagram of the data flow and the security questionnaire you requested.

Next steps I propose: 1) I'll circulate this note and a short FAQ doc; 2) if acceptable, schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi next week to walk the architecture; 3) HealthNova to indicate which region and retention policy you'd like for the POC.

Thanks — Soojin

Thanks Soojin — very helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our privacy team so we can sign off on a short POC: 

- When you say prompts are "not persisted by default," does Redwood keep any transient cache (KV cache) that could contain raw prompts and be flushed? How long does that live?
- For persisted outputs: are they stored with direct identifiers (email, account id) or are outputs stored as blobs with a separate index?
- If we request EU residency, do copies ever exist in the US for backup/analytics?

We can share our SOC 2 checklist if helpful. Also would like the security questionnaire file you mentioned.

Best,

Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt output PII — storage, residency, and TTL Q&A

Hi Maria — answers inline to keep it compact. Apologies for the dense note; happy to walk through live.

Q: KV cache and transient copies?
A: We use in-memory KV caches on the serving nodes to accelerate generation. These caches are ephemeral (RAM-backed) and are never written to disk in hosted mode. They are flushed per-session and have a max lifetime of 5 minutes of inactivity by default. For Dedicated/Private customers you can opt to run with disabled shared caching or run caches within your VPC so nothing leaves your network.

Q: How are persisted outputs indexed/stored?
A: Persisted outputs are stored as encrypted blobs (AES-256-GCM) and indexed by an opaque key; we do not write direct customer PII into the index. Customers can opt to include their own identifiers in metadata if you want easier lookups; otherwise we suggest using mapping keys you control.

Q: EU residency — any US copies?
A: For accounts set to EU residency we provision regionally isolated storage and backups within the EU. No copies are replicated to the US for hosted accounts unless you explicitly request multi-region failover. We provide a written attestation for the POC if needed.

Additional details you may need:
- Default retention: telemetry/metrics 30 days; persisted outputs (if enabled) configurable 30/60/90 days.
- Audit logs: retained 13 months; exportable in CSV/JSON.
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports CMK via partner integrations on enterprise plans.
- Masking: We offer client-side SDK helpers to strip high-risk fields (SSNs, credit card numbers) before sending. We also support server-side redaction rules as part of Redwood Optimize.

Attachments: security_questionnaire_v2.pdf (filled) and redwood-data-map.png (diagram).

If this all looks reasonable, can we confirm EU vs US and your default retention for the POC? Also proposing Rishi do a 45-min technical call Wednesday 8/18 at 10am PT.

Thanks — Soojin

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@healthnova.co>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt output PII — storage, residency, and TTL Q&A

Quick technical confirmation from infra/security side: 
- Model weights never persist customer prompts or outputs; training pipelines are separate and isolated. We do not use customer data for model training unless you sign an explicit agreement.
- KV cache items are RAM-only; if you prefer we can set TTL to 0 for your POC nodes so nothing persists even in memory after request completion.
- Network: all egress to third-party telemetry/analytics is opt-in; default hosted telemetry is internal for SLOs and anonymized.

I can walk through the architecture diagram on Wednesday and show the region isolation and KMS flow.

—Rishi
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
